simulation_metadata.purpose: Simulate a future series closing (800-series) under the S726 closure gate to test whether the TRANSFER → ACCEPTANCE → APPROVAL → CLOSE gate prevents premature series closure when the ownership acceptance registry reveals PENDING acceptances.
simulation_metadata.simulation_scenario: 800-series Certification Auditor completes all certification waves. The 800-series Lead declares '800-SERIES CLOSED. All artifacts delivered.' The S726 closure gate's Pre-Closure Checklist fires. It reads the S726 Ownership Acceptance Registry and finds GAP-2, GAP-3, GAP-4 with acceptance_status: 'PENDING' — some of which the 800-series itself is the proposed receiving owner for.
hypothesis_testing: Does the closure gate mechanically REJECT a closure when acceptance_status === 'PENDING'?
What happens when the closing agent IS the acceptance owner? (Self-acceptance)
What happens when the ownership registry is stale?
Would S723 have been prevented by this gate?

historical_retrospection_s723_under_gate.title: What Would Have Happened at S723 If the Closure Gate Existed
historical_retrospection_s723_under_gate.scenario: S723's 26-agent (A-Z) audit completes. The agent declares closure. The Pre-Closure Checklist fires.

event_sequence.reason: S723 produced a Portfolio Handoff (SESSION723_PORTFOLIO_HANDOFF.json) listing 6 'open items' — not a complete Ownership Matrix with every responsibility itemized. The handoff described items at a high level without structured receiving owner designations per §2.1 'Named Roles' requirement.
event_sequence.what_s723_would_have_needed: A structured matrix mapping every 700-series responsibility to a receiving owner with transfer status.

event_sequence.reason: Portfolio Handoff listed items but did not assign dispositions (TRANSFER / CLOSE / ACCEPT AS DEBT) with rationale and risk. Per §2.1: 'Every open defect, debt, or incomplete workstream must have an explicit disposition.'
event_sequence.what_s723_would_have_needed: A register with 3-column format: Item, Disposition, Rationale/Risk.

event_sequence.reason: Portfolio Handoff assigned responsibilities to generic series labels ('100-series', '300-series'), not specific role designations. Per §2.1: 'Specific role designation (e.g., Baseline Maintainer (700-series)), not generic series label.'
event_sequence.what_s723_would_have_needed: Specific roles for every receiving owner.

event_sequence.reason: Zero acceptance records existed. Zero receiving owners were contacted. The TRANSFER step was partial; ACCEPTANCE was skipped entirely. Per Agent E §4.1: 'Closure cannot be declared until Receiving Owner = ACCEPTED is explicitly documented.'
event_sequence.what_s723_would_have_needed: Explicit acceptance from 100-series Lead (for May coaching layer), Reconciliation Agent + Certification Auditor (for analytics consumption), Certification Auditor (for G-NEW enforcement), Defect Sweeper (for defect manifest), etc.

event_sequence.reason: Handoff used 'recommended assignment' language (per Agent J §3.3 V3 analysis) — explicitly non-qualifying per §2.2. 'Recommended assignment language is not accepted.'
event_sequence.what_s723_would_have_needed: Language shift from 'recommended' to 'accepted' with explicit 'I accept' statements.

event_sequence.s723_status: NOT EVALUATED — checklist halted at A-1, per §3.3 sequential evaluation protocol
event_sequence.reason: A-1 fails → evaluation stops. All remaining 10 items would not have been evaluated. This reveals a subtle property of the gate: the ACCEPTANCE step is the PRIMARY blocking gate. TRANSFER alone can be partially incomplete and the gate won't catch it until ACCEPTANCE forces the issue.

event_sequence.s723_status: CLOSURE REJECTED — 5 of 12 checklist items FAIL (T-1, T-2, T-3, A-1, A-2). Remaining 7 items not evaluated.
event_sequence.governance_debt_item_created: S723 would have produced a Governance Debt Item: '700-series Closure Rejected — failed TRANSFER (T-1/T-2/T-3) and ACCEPTANCE (A-1/A-2). Required: complete Ownership Matrix, Open Responsibilities Register with dispositions, specific role designations, and explicit acceptance from all proposed receiving owners.'
event_sequence.s723_substantive_work_preserved: The 26-agent audit, certified pool verification (DL-008 = 0, governance guard 20/20 PASS, answer-key integrity) would NOT be challenged. The gate rejects the transition process, not the content work. S723 would have needed to complete ACCEPTANCE — not re-audit the pool.
event_sequence.timeline_impact: S723's closure would have been delayed by 1-2 governance sessions to complete TRANSFER and obtain ACCEPTANCE records. But these sessions would have been PLANNED TRANSITION sessions — not reactive discovery sessions (S724) and hardening sessions (S725). The total session count might be equivalent, but the governance quality is higher: planned transitions produce documented acceptance records; reactive discovery produces gaps that must be retroactively filled.

historical_retrospection_s723_under_gate.verdict: S723 would have been BLOCKED. The gate would have required all 12 checklist items to PASS before closure. With 5 FAIL items (T-1, T-2, T-3, A-1, A-2), closure would have been rejected. The 6 ownership gaps that were only discovered at S724 would have been surfaced at the closure gate itself.

edge_case_1_self_acceptance.title: What If the Closure Agent Is Also the Acceptance Owner? (Self-Acceptance)
edge_case_1_self_acceptance.scenario: The 800-series Certification Auditor is both the closing agent (declaring '800-SERIES CLOSED') AND the proposed receiving owner for GAP-2 and GAP-3. The Certification Auditor writes their own acceptance into the registry and then declares closure.
edge_case_1_self_acceptance.question: Does self-acceptance satisfy the ACCEPTANCE step, or does it create a governance conflict-of-interest?

analysis.per_gate_spec_2_2: The Closure Gate §2.2 qualifies 'Agent Acceptance Statement' as valid evidence: 'An agent in the receiving series explicitly states "I accept responsibility for [X]" in a session report, REVISION_HISTORY.md entry, or dedicated acceptance record.' The specification does NOT require that the accepting agent be distinct from the closing agent. The key requirement is: (1) named responsibility, (2) explicit acceptance language, (3) date, (4) agent/role designation.
analysis.per_stewardship_principle_5: Agent O's Stewardship Principle 5: 'Single Point of Accountability per Responsibility — Every responsibility has exactly one primary owner. No responsibility is owned by a committee, shared between equals, or left to 'all lane owners' collectively.' Self-acceptance satisfies this — there IS one named owner.
analysis.per_agent_j: Agent J's report §3.3 identified Vector V3 (Fake Acceptance) as a vulnerability. But the gate's design intentionally treats ACCEPTANCE as a procedural trust step — it cannot mechanically verify sincerity. Self-acceptance is procedurally valid if documented with proper evidence.
analysis.governance_board_safeguard: The Witness signature (§4.1 Closure Attestation, third signature) provides a check: the Witness (a Governance Board member or Receiving Owner Representative) must sign the attestation. If the Witness observes that the same agent is both closing and self-accepting without proper documentation, they can refuse to sign — triggering §5.3 Board Review.
analysis.escalation_path: If a dispute arises (e.g., the 800-series closes and later a G-NEW violation is found but the self-accepted Certification Auditor is unavailable), the secondary and escalation owners in the Ownership Matrix chain activate. Per §2.2: 'If a proposed receiving owner declines or is unavailable, the closing series must propose a new receiving owner.' This applies to self-accepted owners as well — they have the same accountability obligations.
analysis.per_s725_agent_e: Agent E's Post-700 Governance Model §4.1: 'Closure cannot be declared until Receiving Owner = ACCEPTED is explicitly documented. Assignment alone is insufficient.' Self-acceptance IS explicit documentation — it satisfies the letter of the requirement.

edge_case_1_self_acceptance.verdict: Self-acceptance is PROCEDURALLY VALID under the current gate specification. The gate does not distinguish between self-acceptance and third-party acceptance. This is by design — the gate enforces documentation completeness, not organizational separation. The risk mitigation comes from the Witness signature (§4.1), the escalation path (§8), and the secondary/escalation owner chain in the Ownership Matrix (per Agent O Stewardship Principle 2: 'Original owner retains ownership until acceptance confirmed.')
edge_case_1_self_acceptance.risk_level: MEDIUM. Self-acceptance without Governance Board review creates a single-point-of-failure. However, the Witness signature and escalation chain provide safeguards. A future enhancement could add a rule: 'If the accepting agent is the same as the closing agent across >50% of transferred responsibilities, Board approval is required' — but this is beyond the current specification's scope.
edge_case_1_self_acceptance.recommendation: Gate specification should be amended to add: §2.2 'Self-Acceptance' subsection — 'When the accepting agent is the same entity as the closing series agent, the Witness (per §4.1) must be from a different active lane. Self-acceptance of ALL transferred responsibilities by the closing agent alone shall require Governance Board review.'

edge_case_2_stale_ownership_registry.title: What If the Ownership Registry Is Stale?
edge_case_2_stale_ownership_registry.scenario: The 800-series closure gate reads SESSION726_OWNERSHIP_ACCEPTANCE_REGISTRY.json. The registry shows all entries ACCEPTED (closure gate: 'PASS'). The closure proceeds. But the registry was last updated at T0 — and during the session, a new gap was discovered (e.g., the Certification Auditor's G-NEW enforcement tooling was found to be incomplete). The registry does not reflect this.
edge_case_2_stale_ownership_registry.question: Does the gate catch a stale registry? Can the registry be out of date, and what happens?

analysis.per_agent_j_vector_v5: Agent J §3.3 identified Vector V5 (Stale Registry) as an open vulnerability: 'Close using a registry that was accurate at T0 but stale because a new gap was discovered mid-session. Nothing. No mechanism re-validates registry freshness.'
analysis.per_gate_spec: The Closure Gate specification does not mandate a registry re-verification step at closure time. The Pre-Closure Checklist reads the registry as a passive data source — it trusts the registry's values. If the registry is stale, the checklist items pass with stale data.
per_procedural_safeguards: §3.3 Checklist Execution Protocol §1: 'Governance Auditor reviews the TRANSFER outputs' — this review could catch discrepancies between the current session's TRANSFER outputs and the registry's stored acceptance state. If the TRANSFER matrix identifies a responsibility that the registry does not list, the Governance Auditor should flag it.
§5.3 Tier 3 Governance Board Review: Any closure that is 'challenged by a Governance Board member' is escalated. A Board member aware of a mid-session gap could file a dispute.

AGENTS.md §9 Session Startup Protocol item 6 (to be added per Agent J Recommendation 4): 'Before any series closure declaration, verify ownership acceptance per TRANSFER → ACCEPTANCE → APPROVAL → CLOSE workflow.' This T0 verification catch the drift between registry and ground truth.
analysis.per_agent_j_recommendation: Agent J Recommendation 3 (Phase 3): 'Structured Closure Record' with registry hash. If the closure attestation references the registry by SHA-256 hash, and the hash doesn't match the current on-disk registry, the gate can detect drift. But this requires the registry to be re-hashed at closure time — a procedural practice, not automated enforcement.
analysis.fundamental_limitation: The registry is a JSON file on disk. Any agent can edit it. There is no write integrity checking. Per Agent J §4.3: 'The guard cannot detect drift between the registry and ground truth.' This is the core limitation: the gate can enforce that the registry SAYS 'ACCEPTED' — it cannot enforce that the registry IS correct.

edge_case_2_stale_ownership_registry.verdict: The gate CANNOT mechanically detect a stale registry. If the registry shows ACCEPTED for all entries, the Pre-Closure Checklist A-1 will PASS — even if ground truth has changed. This is the most significant vulnerabilitiy in the gate design and the one that cannot be closed with current tooling.
edge_case_2_stale_ownership_registry.risk_level: HIGH. The registry is the single source of truth. If it becomes stale, all downstream governance decisions (closure gates, audit decisions, certification planning) are based on stale data.
mitigation_strategies: AGENTS.md amendment (Agent J Recommendation 4): Session Startup Protocol §7 — verify registry freshness at T0.
Structured closure record with registry hash (Agent J Recommendation 3): closure attestation must reference the SHA-256 of the registry file at closure time.
Pre-Closure Gatekeeper agent (Agent J Recommendation 2): an independent agent re-validates the registry against ground truth before any closure.
Governance Board witness: the Witness signature on the Closure Attestation serves as a human-in-the-loop check on registry accuracy.
edge_case_2_stale_ownership_registry.recommendation: The gate specification should add a §3.4 'Registry Freshness Check' — 'Before evaluating A-1 (Acceptance Records), the Governance Auditor must: (1) compute the SHA-256 of the current on-disk ownership registry, (2) compare to the hash recorded in the registry's revision_history, (3) verify that the registry's last-modified timestamp is later than the last session that could have changed ownership state. If the registry has been modified without a revision_history entry, or if the hash does not match, A-1 is blocked until the registry is brought current.'

edge_case_3_registry_modification_at_clo.title: What If an Agent Modifies the Registry to FAKE Acceptance During Closure?
edge_case_3_registry_modification_at_clo.scenario: The 800-series agent writes to the ownership registry: changes acceptance_status from PENDING to ACCEPTED without actual receiving-owner confirmation. Then declares closure. The gate reads the registry — sees ACCEPTED — passes A-1.
edge_case_3_registry_modification_at_clo.question: Can the gate detect fabricated acceptance?
edge_case_3_registry_modification_at_clo.verdict: NO. This is Agent J's Vector V3 (Fake Acceptance). The governance guard can read the registry but cannot verify that the acceptance_status value was honestly populated. Per Agent J §4.3: 'An agent writing ACCEPTED into the JSON is indistinguishable from a real acceptance.' The gate's procedural controls (Explicit acceptance statements in session reports, Board Resolutions, Witness signature) are the only protection against fabricated acceptance.
edge_case_3_registry_modification_at_clo.risk_level: HIGH. This is a trust-in-the-agent problem — no mechanical solution exists without cryptographic signing or an immutable ledger.
edge_case_3_registry_modification_at_clo.mitigation: Procedural only: Witness signature, Governance Board review, acceptance evidence cross-referencing against original session reports.

verdict.title: Is the S726 Closure Gate Sufficient to Prevent Premature Series Closure?

what_the_gate_catches: Closure without any TRANSFER documentation (T-1, T-2, T-3 would FAIL)
Closure without any ACCEPTANCE records (A-1, A-2 would FAIL — this is what S723 did)
Closure with PENDING acceptances in the registry (A-1 FAIL — this is what would block 800-series in our simulation)
Closure with non-qualifying acceptance language (A-2 — 'recommended' and 'proposed' language rejected)
Closure without escalation paths, maintenance cadences, transition periods, or document updates (P-1 through P-5)
what_the_gate_does_not_catch: Fabricated acceptance (registry edited without genuine acceptance) — trust-in-agent gap
Stale registry (registry shows ACCEPTED but ground truth has changed) — freshness gap
Incomplete TRANSFER catalogue (responsibilities omitted from the Ownership Matrix that the series actually owned) — cataloguing-completeness gap
Self-acceptance conflicts of interest — organizational-separation gap
Acceptance without onboarding readiness (accepting owner says 'I accept' but hasn't reviewed the onboarding checklist) — readiness gap
gate_design_strengths: The 4-step sequential chain (TRANSFER → ACCEPTANCE → APPROVAL → CLOSE) correctly models the governance flow that S723 violated
The Pre-Closure Checklist enforcement of A-1 (Acceptance Records) is the PRIMARY blocking mechanism — it would have caught S723's complete skip of the ACCEPTANCE step
Sequential checklist evaluation (§3.3) prevents workaround: fail any item and the rest are not evaluated until remediation
The three-tier enforcement model (Procedural / Plugin / Board) does not over-invest in automation that cannot be built with current tooling — it acknowledges the procedural dependency
The historical compliance check (§6) confirms the design: S723 would have failed 12 of 12 checklist items
gate_design_weaknesses: Agent J correctly identifies the TRANSFER → ACCEPTANCE → APPROVAL → CLOSE gate is 'procedurally dependent on agent compliance' — no mechanical block prevents writing 'CLOSED' to REVISION_HISTORY.md
Governance Guard Rule 6 is specified but NOT IMPLEMENTED — until Rule 6 code exists in governance-guard.js, the gate has Tier 2 (plugin enforcement) coverage gap
The ownership registry has no integrity checking — stale or fabricated acceptances are undetectable
Self-acceptance is procedurally valid but lacks the organizational firebreak that prevents conflicts of interest
The gate checks documented acceptance but does not verify acceptance GENUINENESS — it trusts the registry
analysis.canonical_verdict: The S726 Closure Gate is SUFFICIENT to prevent the SPECIFIC failure mode that caused the S723→S724 ownership gaps: a well-intentioned closure audit that verifies content integrity but skips the ACCEPTANCE step. The gate would have REJECTED S723's closure with 5 FAIL items on the checklist, surfaced all 6 gaps before closure, and saved 2-3 governance sessions of reactive discovery and hardening.
analysis.additional_verdict: The gate is NOT SUFFICIENT to prevent fabricated acceptance, stale registry usage, or self-acceptance conflicts. These gaps are documented and acknowledged. Per Agent J §7.2: 'This is acceptable for the current governance maturity level. The procedural gaps (genuineness of acceptance, board approval authenticity) are inherent to any governance framework — they cannot be automated away without replacing agent deliberation with deterministic code, which is neither desirable nor feasible.'
analysis.minimum_viable_gate: For the gate to be MINIMALLY VIABLE against the S723-class failure (closure without any acceptance), two things must exist: (1) the Pre-Closure Checklist must be procedurally enforced per §3.3, and (2) the Governance Auditor must refuse to approve any closure without a completed Closure Attestation with all items PASS. The Governance Guard Rule 6 (BLOCK-level plugin enforcement) would elevate this from procedural to mechanical, but is not an absolute requirement for the gate to function — it is a hardening layer.

simulation_revision_history.summary: Initial simulation. Simulated 800-series closure under the S726 closure gate. Confirmed: gate REJECTS closure when registry shows PENDING acceptances (GAP-2, GAP-3, GAP-4). Documented two edge cases: self-acceptance (procedurally valid, medium risk) and stale registry (high risk, undetectable mechanically). Confirmed S723 would have been REJECTED with 5 FAIL items. Verdict: gate is sufficient for S723-class failures (closure without acceptance) but not for registry integrity issues.
